ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle EDF, with vertex F above, and E and D at the two ends of the base. Point Q is located on side ED, and EQ and QD have the same double tick marks, indicating EQ = QD, so Q is the midpoint of ED. Segment FQ connects from vertex F to the midpoint Q of side ED, and passes through point T. The problem text states that T is the centroid of triangle EDF, and FT = 12. Reasoning: Because Q is the midpoint of ED, FQ is the median from vertex F to the opposite side ED. The centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio in the direction from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, so FT:TQ = 2:1. Given FT = 12, therefore TQ = 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

raw_record.question_text: In $\triangle EDF$, $T$ is the centroid and $FT=12$. Find $TQ$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle EDF has point Q on side ED, with matching tick marks on EQ and QD showing Q is the midpoint of ED; the segment FQ is drawn and passes through T. Read from the text that T is the centroid and FT = 12, and the target is TQ. Use the centroid theorem: a centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio measured from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. Since FQ is the median from vertex F to midpoint Q, FT:TQ = 2:1. Therefore TQ = 12/2 = 6.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: Q is marked as the midpoint of ED, and the line from F to Q contains T, so FQ is the median through the centroid. From the text, T is the centroid and FT = 12. Instead of using the ratio only locally, compute the entire median length: for a centroid, the distance from the vertex to the centroid is two-thirds of the median, so FT = (2/3)FQ. With FT = 12, solve FQ = 18. Then TQ is the remaining part of the median, so TQ = FQ - FT = 18 - 12 = 6.
